description: A Vue/vis-network prototype represents a chat as editable graph nodes and edges, with a blank child node filled from its parent-message chain through an OpenAI-compatible endpoint.
scope_audience: The README describes a prototype for one local user with a compatible server; it is explicitly not presented as a product and has no persistence.

creativity.reason: Treating graph topology as conversation state is an interesting interaction model, but the README gives no evidence of a distinctive or globally novel contribution.

current_usefulness.reason: Graph editing and response generation are implemented in the component, but the code hardcodes the endpoint, does not persist state, and its own README lists incomplete streaming/API seams.

expected_usefulness.reason: If completed with reliable branching, persistence, and configurable generation, the graph could help a user explore alternate chat paths; no tested advantage over linear/threaded chat is established.

impl_progress.reason: Graph creation, editing, edge linking, subtree deletion, and ancestor-message requests exist in GraphCanvas.vue; no tests, persistence, backend, or executed UI evidence was found.

presentability.reason: README explains purpose and setup but labels the project deprecated, with no persistence/tests/configuration and a fixed local endpoint; no visual demo was inspected.

delivery_likelihood.reason: The prototype is archived and has no active roadmap; the basic interaction exists, but persistence and reliable response handling are not evidenced.

verification: Inspected README and GraphCanvas component only; no build, tests, API call, or browser session.

createBubble; deleteBubbleAndChildren; triggerGeneration; saveEdit; onMounted graph handlers

contribution: A graph-native chat sketch makes branches, edits, and parent context visible as editable edges and nodes rather than a transcript-only interface.
alternatives_question: Which chat products or open-source interfaces use an editable node graph as the conversation state, and do they preserve branch context and make alternate reasoning easier on the same task?
reason: The core interaction is implemented and worth preserving as a prototype, but there is no evidence of durable or dependable use and the archive status is explicit.
next_step: If the graph-chat idea remains in scope, validate one end-to-end branching task and decide whether persistence and endpoint configuration are required before further polish.
